candidate.derivedAnswer: D. They are not necessarily the same.
candidate.answerReason: For \(U=\{1,2\}\), \(A=\{1\}\), and \(B=\{2\}\), the intersection of the complements is empty, but the complement of the intersection is \(U\). Thus the two operations need not agree.

methods.label: Finite counterexample
methods.explanation:
Use the same universal set \(U\) for both expressions: \(A^c\cap B^c\) and \((A\cap B)^c\). A single counterexample is enough to show that they do not always agree.

Let \(U=\{1,2\}\), \(A=\{1\}\), and \(B=\{2\}\). Then \(A^c=\{2\}\) and \(B^c=\{1\}\), so
\[
A^c\cap B^c=\varnothing.
\]
But \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), so
\[
(A\cap B)^c=U=\{1,2\}.
\]
The results differ, so they are not necessarily the same. The answer is D.
methods.levelReason: Evaluates elementary set operations on two-element sets and refutes an always-claim with one counterexample.
